title: Coefficient pullback preserves the equations and embedded Proj of a homogeneous quotient
statement: Let $U$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], $n\geq0$, $\mathcal S=\mathcal O_U[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ with variables of degree one, and $J\subseteq\mathcal S$ a quasi-coherent homogeneous ideal; degree-zero equations are allowed and no finite generation is assumed. Put $\mathcal B=\mathcal S/J$ with its quotient grading [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], $Z=\operatorname{Proj}_U\mathcal B$ [def-nagata-relative-proj], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_U$ be the closed immersion induced by the quotient map [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. For any scheme morphism $g:T\to U$, let $J_T$ be the image of $g^*J\to g^*\mathcal S\cong\mathcal O_T[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$, using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. There is a canonical graded algebra isomorphism $g^*\mathcal B\cong\mathcal O_T[x_0,\ldots,x_n]/J_T$. On affine tests $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq U$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq g^{-1}V$, it is the isomorphism $R'\otimes_R(R[x]/J_V)\cong R'[x]/(\operatorname{image}J_V)$ sending $r'\otimes\bar p$ to $r'\overline{p_{R'}}$, where $J_V=\Gamma(V,J)$ and $p_{R'}$ is the coefficientwise image of $p$. The canonical relative-Proj isomorphisms for $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal S$ make the square with top arrow $\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal O_T[x]/J_T)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$, bottom arrow $i$, and the two base-change projections cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. On every coordinate chart the comparison sends a homogeneous fraction $b/x_j^d$ to $b_{R'}/x_j^d$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]; thus it identifies the specified embeddings as closed subschemes. In every degree $d$, the affine pullback component is $R'\otimes_R\Gamma(V,\mathcal B_d)$. No flatness of $g$ or injectivity of $g^*J\to g^*\mathcal S$ is required; only its image ideal is used.

source.place: Agent-extracted interface for former proof step 6 of lem-sfb-flat-graded-tail-proj: Constructions Tag 01O3 (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), canonical chart maps and their naturality for the graded polynomial quotient. The tensor-quotient and embedding compatibility arguments, not an additional abstract base-change theorem, are preserved in the report.

proof.text: Work over affine tests $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq g^{-1}V$. The quasi-coherent cokernel/image theorem applied to $J\to\mathcal S$ identifies $\Gamma(V,\mathcal B)$ with $A=R[x]/I$, $I=J(V)$, degree by degree. Pullbacks of the quasi-coherent modules $J,\mathcal S,\mathcal B_d$ are quasi-coherent. The affine pullback theorem identifies their sections on $W$ with the corresponding $R'$-tensors, naturally in the module maps. Applying the cokernel/image theorem on $T$ identifies $J_T(W)$ with the image of $R'\otimes_R I\to R'\otimes_R R[x]$. These assertions have no flatness or finite-type hypotheses.

Identify $R'\otimes_R R[x]$ with $R'[x]$ by $a\otimes p\mapsto a p_{R'}$. The inverse sends $\sum_\alpha a_\alpha x^\alpha$ to $\sum_\alpha a_\alpha\otimes x^\alpha$. Balancing and uniqueness of the finite monomial expansion show that the composites are identities; multiplication is respected since $x^\alpha x^\beta=x^{\alpha+\beta}$. Both maps preserve total degree and the unit. Under this identification, the image in step 1 is the set of finite sums $\sum a_k(p_k)_{R'}$ with $p_k\in I$. This set is an ideal: multiplication by a coefficient is immediate, and multiplication by $x_j$ replaces $p_k$ by $x_jp_k\in I$. It therefore equals the ideal $I'$ generated by the coefficient images of $I$. It is homogeneous by decomposing each $p_k$ into its homogeneous components, all of which lie in $I$.

source.place: Tag 01O3 (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), coefficient pullback; explicit polynomial algebra calculation supplementing the source

proof.text: Construct $\Phi:R'\otimes_R A\to R'[x]/I'$ by $a\otimes\bar p\mapsto a\overline{p_{R'}}$. Changing $p$ by an element of $I$ changes the output by zero; balancing follows from coefficient substitution. For the inverse, send each coefficient $a\in R'$ to $a\otimes1$ and each variable $x_j$ to $1\otimes\bar x_j$, obtaining a polynomial algebra homomorphism $R'[x]\to R'\otimes_R A$. Each $p_{R'}$ with $p\in I$ maps to $1\otimes\bar p=0$, so the homomorphism factors through $I'$. The inverse composite on $a\otimes\bar p$ is $a(1\otimes\bar p)$, and the other composite fixes all coefficients and variables. These generate the respective algebras, proving both inverse identities. The formulas preserve degree, products and the unit. This proves the required graded quotient isomorphism without assuming that $R'\otimes_R I\to R'\otimes_R R[x]$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), quotient right exactness; explicit mutually inverse algebra maps giving its polynomial specialization

proof.text: The maps just constructed commute with restrictions of affine tests: on a pure tensor both restriction-then-comparison and comparison-then-restriction send $a\otimes\bar p$ to the restricted coefficient $a$ times the quotient class of the restricted polynomial $p$. The inverse maps likewise agree on coefficients and variables. Naturality of the affine pullback identification in step 1 gives the same restriction maps on the sheaf side. Thus the maps and their inverses glue on affine refinements of all overlaps, giving $g^*\mathcal B\cong\mathcal O_T[x]/J_T$ as graded algebra sheaves. In degree $d$, apply the affine pullback theorem to the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal B_d$ to obtain precisely $R'\otimes_R\Gamma(V,\mathcal B_d)$. The quasi-coherent cokernel/image theorem ensures that the quotient and image sheaves used here are quasi-coherent. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine.

source.place: Tags 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent); affine restriction and sheaf gluing

proof.text: The maps $\mathcal S\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal O_T[x]\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_T[x]/J_T$ are surjective graded maps of quasi-coherent algebras. Clause 3 of relative-Proj functoriality gives the specified closed immersions on their Proj schemes. This uses the surjection clause, not its flat-base-change clause. On a coordinate chart, their comorphisms are the quotient localization maps $p/x_j^d\mapsto\bar p/\bar x_j^d$: changing a fraction representative preserves this formula because the defining relation is an equality after multiplying by a power of $x_j$, and a ring homomorphism preserves that equality. The coordinate opens cover: every positive-degree monomial has a variable factor, so the images of the variables generate the irrelevant ideal. This is also valid if a variable image is nilpotent, in which case its chart is empty.

Apply arbitrary relative-Proj base change separately to $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal B$. With the graded identifications of steps 2--4, and the induced Proj isomorphism for a graded isomorphism, this gives $\mathbf P^n_T\cong T\times_U\mathbf P^n_U$ and $Z_T:=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal O_T[x]/J_T)\cong T\times_U Z$. To identify their actual comparison maps, apply affine-Proj scalar extension on $V,W$ to $R[x]$ and $A$. Its chart formula sends $b/x_j^d$ to $b_{R'}/x_j^d$. Here $b_{R'}$ means the image of $1\otimes b$ under the graded isomorphism of step 3; this is independent of any polynomial lift. The same formula for the polynomial algebra uses step 2. Thus these are the canonical relative-Proj comparisons, specified on the standard charts, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms of the underlying schemes.

Check compatibility with the embeddings on every $x_j$ chart. A fraction $p/x_j^d$ in the ambient chart ring has two images in the quotient chart over $W$: quotient first and then coefficient substitution gives $\overline{p_{R'}}/x_j^d$, while coefficient substitution first and then quotient gives exactly $\overline{p_{R'}}/x_j^d$. The maps also agree on $R'$-coefficients. Pure tensors of these fractions generate the scalar-extended chart ring additively, so this proves equality of the two chart comorphisms. The chart description of affine-Proj scalar extension and the cover in step 5 therefore identify the top embedding with $\mathrm{id}_T\times_U i$. Equality holds as scheme morphisms, not merely on points: it is equality on each affine chart ring. Consequently the specified closed subschemes and their chart fraction coordinates agree.

source.place: Tags 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj) and 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj): explicit commutation of the coefficient and quotient chart maps

proof.text: Finally the square $T\times_U Z\to T\times_U\mathbf P^n_U$ above $i:Z\to\mathbf P^n_U$ is cartesian by the fibre-product universal property. Indeed a test scheme $H$ mapping to $Z$ by $a$ and to $T\times_U\mathbf P^n_U$ by $(t,p)$ with $i a=p$ determines the unique pair $(t,a):H\to T\times_U Z$; the compatibility over $U$ follows by composing $i a=p$ with $\mathbf P^n_U\to U$. Its projections are the required maps, and any other factorization has the same $t,a$, hence is equal. Transport this square through the canonical isomorphisms and the equality of embeddings in steps 6--7. This proves the asserted cartesian square and completes all clauses, including arbitrary $J$ and arbitrary $g$.
